title: Critical Mineral Consistency Act of 2025
official_title: To amend the Energy Act of 2020 to harmonize the lists of critical minerals and critical materials, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Ciscomani (R-AZ) with 13 cosponsors from both parties; passed the House and was placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar. The change is a technical, list-harmonization change with bipartisan backing, which improves its odds of a Senate vote.
summary: Creates a single 'Critical Minerals and Materials List' that combines the critical minerals designated under existing law with the critical materials the Energy Department has determined, and requires it to be published within 45 days of enactment and updated quickly after any designation change.
brief: Amends the Energy Act of 2020 to create a combined 'Critical Minerals and Materials List,' published within 45 days of enactment and updated within 45 days of any critical-mineral or critical-material designation change.

top_lines.headline: Critical Minerals and Materials List
subs: Creates a combined 'Critical Minerals and Materials List' of designated critical minerals and determined critical materials
List must be updated within 45 days of a new designation
Amends Section 7002 of the Energy Act of 2020

items.main: Names the Act the “Critical Mineral Consistency Act of 2025”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Critical Minerals and Materials List

items.main: Amends the Energy Act of 2020 to create a new 'Critical Minerals and Materials List' that combines the critical minerals designated under subsection (c) with the critical materials the Secretary of Energy has determined.
items.detail: Adds a new subsection (o) to Section 7002 of the Energy Act of 2020 (30 U.S.C. 1606), redesignates the existing subsection (o) as (p), and inserts 'minerals or materials' after 'critical' in subsection (c)(4)(C). Within 45 days of enactment, the Secretary must publish a Critical Minerals and Materials List combining designated critical minerals and determined critical materials, and must update it within 45 days of any critical-mineral or critical-material designation change. The Secretary and the Secretary of Energy are to coordinate on updates to the maximum extent practicable, and Federal agencies that incorporate the 'critical mineral' or 'critical material' definition must use the most recently published version of the list.

gaps: The bill combines critical minerals and critical materials into a single published list but does not change what benefits or requirements attach to either designation.
It requires the list to be updated within 45 days of a designation change but specifies no separate process or deadline for removing materials no longer considered critical.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Stauber
featured_quotes.text: While the respective lists developed by the U.S. Geological Survey and the Department of Energy have been helpful in ensuring we have policies in place that increase and stabilize our access to these critical minerals and materials, they are not hitting the mark and require further direction from Congress. The two agencies use different criteria and do not take into consideration the same parameters, sometimes leading to different lists.
